Article Title: Jharkhand student protest: Govt to hold fresh talks as fasting student leader's health worsens
Article Text:
Jharkhand exam stir: Govt to hold fresh talks; health of student leader on fast deteriorates (PTI image)

NEW DELHI: The Jharkhand government will hold another round of talks with protesting recruitment exam aspirants on Sunday, as the 16-day agitation continued and the health of student leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who has been on an indefinite hunger strike for nearly a week, deteriorated.The decision to hold a sixth round of talks came after discussions between the government and several student groups over Friday and Saturday failed to break the deadlock.Mahto's condition suddenly worsened around 3 am on Sunday at Ranchi's Jaipal Singh Stadium, where students have been protesting since July 25. Doctors recorded his blood glucose level at 53.The government panel is scheduled to meet student representatives at noon on Sunday. The move, however, has drawn criticism from the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch, which has been leading the agitation.Ravindra Paswan, a leader of the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch, accused the government of trying to divide the protesting students and divert attention from their demands."This is political manoeuvring by the government. It is trying to create a divide among students and divert attention. But they should know that all students are united," Paswan said at a press conference at the Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium.Paswan claimed that the Reforms Manch had already presented its demands to the five-member government panel during a detailed meeting on Friday night. He alleged that the government subsequently held separate discussions with other student organisations that had not played a role in the ongoing protest.Govt says talks held in positive atmosphereThe Hemant Soren government held discussions with the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch on Friday night, followed by four rounds of talks with different student groups on Saturday.The groups included the Congress-backed National Students' Union of India (NSUI), Jharkhand Chhatra Morcha (JCM) and Adivasi Chhatra Sangh (ACS).The government said the discussions were held in a positive atmosphere and that it was examining the concerns raised by the protesting aspirants.The decision to hold another round of talks was taken after the government panel met Chief Minister Hemant Soren for around four hours on Saturday evening.Rural Development Minister Dipika Pandey Singh said the panel briefed the chief minister about the demands raised by different student delegations."It was decided in the meeting with the chief minister that a final round of talks with the protesting students will take place at 12 pm on Sunday," she said.Minister Sanjay Prasad Yadav said the government would continue discussions with students demanding comprehensive reforms in the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC).What are students demanding?The protesting students are seeking reforms in the recruitment examination system and action over alleged irregularities in various JPSC and JSSC examinations.The JCM submitted five demands, including cancellation of the 14th JPSC Civil Services Examination.The NSUI submitted six demands, including a CID investigation into all JPSC and JSSC examinations under suspicion within 90 days. It also demanded the establishment of a Jharkhand Testing Agency on the lines of the National Testing Agency.The ACS demanded that tribal and regional languages be included as qualifying papers in recruitment examinations. It also sought cancellation of examinations in which irregularities were found.Higher and Technical Education Minister Sudivya Kumar said the government had also issued an email ID through which aspirants could submit suggestions on reforms to the recruitment process.Protesters threaten Assembly marchDespite the government's talks with various student groups, protesters have said the agitation will continue until their demands are met.They have announced a march to the Jharkhand Assembly on August 10 if the government fails to address their demands by Sunday.The agitation has also seen the involvement of several student organisations, including the All India Students' Association (AISA) and Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP).AISA set up a separate platform at the stadium on Saturday, although its leaders said it should not be viewed as a separate agitation.AISA national president Neha Bora, who was attacked with ink during Friday's Assembly march near Birsa Chowk, briefly joined the protest and raised slogans demanding cancellation of the 14th JPSC and JSSC-CGL examinations.AISA's Ranchi unit chief Vijay Kumar said the organisation shared the same demands as the larger protest and that its members would join the August 10 march without carrying the AISA banner.The ABVP has also held protests over the issue. Its members scuffled with police on Friday while attempting to cross barricades near the chief minister's residence.Around eight to 10 ABVP protesters were detained during the march but were later released, Deputy Superintendent of Police (Headquarters) Ajay Aryan said.The ABVP has announced a separate march to the Assembly on August 11.19 arrested over alleged exam irregularitiesThe agitation comes amid an investigation into alleged irregularities in JPSC examinations.Nineteen people have so far been arrested in connection with the case, while former JPSC panel chairperson L Khiangte has been questioned four times since July 28.With the student leader's health deteriorating and protesters threatening another Assembly march, Sunday's talks could prove crucial in determining whether the 16-day agitation can be brought to an end or enters another phase of confrontation.
Article Summary: Jharkhand government to hold sixth round of talks with protesting students on Sunday. Health of student leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who has been on an indefinite hunger strike for nearly a week, has deteriorated. Students are seeking reforms in the recruitment examination system and action over alleged irregularities in various examinations.

Article Title: Amit Shah presents President's Colour to Puducherry Police
Article Text:
Union home minister Amit Shah on Sunday presented the prestigious President’s Colours to the Puducherry Police in a glittering ceremony.

PUDUCHERRY: Union home minister Amit Shah presented the President's Colour to Puducherry Police on Sunday.Shah presented the honour to the Union Territory's uniformed force's Ensign Officer at an official event held at the Puducherry Armed Police Ground in neighbouring Gorimedu. Shah was accompanied by DGP Shalini Singh.Lt Governor K Kailashnathan and chief minister N Rangasamy, among others were present.President Droupadi Murmu had announced on May 8 the conferment of the honour (Nishaan) on Puducherry police in recognition of its "exceptional service, discipline and distinguished achievements".The President's Colour is the highest honour given to a military unit or police of a state or union territory.Past recipients of the honour include the Indian Navy, Indian Coast Guard and various state police departments.
Article Summary: Shah presented the honour to the Union Territory's uniformed force's Ensign Officer at an official event held at the Puducherry Armed Police Ground in neighbouring Gorimedu. The President's Colour is the highest honour given to a military unit or police of a state or union territory.Past recipients of the honour include the Indian Navy, Indian Coast Guard and various state police departments.

Article Title: Gen Z is a force that can’t be ignored: Dharmendra Pradhan
Article Text:
Pradhan said he “suffered” because of Gen Z’s stubbornness but had come to realise that the new generation must be understood rather than resisted

BHUBANESWAR: Former Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan on Saturday described Gen Z as a force that cannot be ignored, saying he had told PM Narendra Modi that the responsibilities of an education minister were insignificant compared to the determination and aspirations of the country’s youth.Speaking in a light-hearted vein, the Sambalpur MP said he “suffered” because of Gen Z’s stubbornness but had come to realise that the new generation must be understood rather than resisted.Though some people tried to mislead Gen Z, Pradhan said, the ministerial position “was not at all a prestige issue for me”. Referring to around 20 crores in the 15-25 age group, Pradhan said, “If 20 crore youngsters become determined about something, my responsibility is nothing before their resolve,” adding that he tried to explain this reality to the PM, who later engaged directly with the youth. “Country’s interest is above all,” he said.The Sambalpur MP said every generation has produced youths who made sacrifices for the country.“Historically, it is the youth who have led change and offered sacrifices. They were the Gen Z of their times,” Pradhan said.
Article Summary: Former Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan described Gen Z as a force that cannot be ignored. He said he had told PM Narendra Modi that the responsibilities of an education minister were insignificant compared to the determination and aspirations of the country’s youth.

Article Title: 21 of 57 TN MPs attend CM Vijay’s meet, reject Delimitation Bill; DMK, AIADMK stay away
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu MPs on Saturday "unanimously" decided to oppose Centre's Delimitation Bill after chief minister C Joseph Vijay chaired a meeting to discuss its likely impact on the state.Congress MP Karti Chidambaram said around 21 out of 57 Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha MPs attended the meeting and agreed to resist any alteration in Tamil Nadu's representation in Parliament."The chief minister of Tamil Nadu had called for a meeting for all the MPs from Tamil Nadu from both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha. About 21 of us attended the meeting, and there was absolute unanimity that Tamil Nadu's rights must be preserved. Our representation in Parliament can't be diminished. Any kind of alteration and delimitation, either on the basis of population or on a proportionate increase, will be resisted," Chidambaram said."We want Parliament to be frozen at 543, and the distribution among the states to be preserved as it is, which means Tamil Nadu will have 39 members in a House of 543. We are clear in our unanimous opinion that a larger Parliament will be an ineffective Parliament, and Tamil Nadu will not be well served by a larger Parliament.So we want Parliament to be preserved at 543 with the same representation of 39 Lok Sabha MPs for Tamil Nadu," he added.The meeting was boycotted by the DMK and AIADMK, which dismissed the deliberations as a "farce" and a "drama".The meeting was held at Kalaivanar Arangam, a government-owned auditorium near the Secretariat.Senior DMK leader A Raja told reporters in Perambalur that it was "a farce, a laughable exercise", arguing that the TVK government was deliberating on an issue about which it had no clarity.Meanwhile, AIADMK called the meeting a "hurriedly staged drama", pointing out that no new delimitation Bill had been introduced in Parliament and there had been no official announcement on the exercise.While the Congress and other opposition parties have supported the Women's Reservation Bill, they have opposed linking its implementation to the delimitation exercise. The opposition has demanded that women's reservation be delinked from delimitation.The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, 2023, was passed by both Houses of Parliament. However, its implementation has not moved forward after the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill fell in the Lok Sabha on April 17, failing to secure the constitutionally required two-thirds majority of members present and voting.The Bill linked the implementation of 33 percent women's reservation in legislatures to delimitation of Lok Sabha constituencies.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu MPs "unanimously" decided to oppose Centre's Delimitation Bill. Meeting was boycotted by DMK and AIADMK, which dismissed deliberations as a "farce" and a "drama" DMK leader A Raja said it was "a farce, a laughable exercise"

Article Title: 6 years after NDA exit, SAD backs delimitation push
Article Text:
Badal's announcement conveyed the government’s efforts to realign the numbers in its favour this time round, after a similar exercise was defeated in the last session by a joint opposition, which has since been considerably weakened

Government likely to bring back delimitation bill , but timing not clear yet

NEW DELHI: A day after his meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Akali Dal president Sukhbir Singh Badal on Saturday reversed his party's earlier opposition to the rollout of the women's reservation law from 2029 with an increase in the Lok Sabha's strength by 50% and supported any fresh move to implement the two together, signalling the possibility of the govt reviving the Constitution amendment bill soon.Akali Dal had walked out of the BJP-led NDA government in September 2020, ending a 23-year-old alliance, due to the Centre's passage of the three farm bills. DMK, another opponent being eyed by the government as a potential supporter of its renewed bid, snubbed governing TVK's all-party meeting on delimitation. NDA is also banking on NCP(SP) to support the measure.While Sukhbir Singh Badal’s party has only one MP — his wife Harsimrat is a Lok Sabha member — his announcement conveyed the government’s efforts to realign the numbers in its favour this time round, after a similar exercise was defeated in the last session by a joint opposition, which has since been considerably weakened.While DMK called it a diversionary tactic and wondered why CM Vijay did not summon the meeting on a pressing issue like the Mekedatu dam row, the party clearly did not want to be part of an exercise to frame delimitation as damaging to the interests of the state, with TVK ally Congress up in arms against it.Developments in governing BJP-led NDA and opposition camps are a clear indication that the government is bringing back the bill, which will need two-thirds support in Parliament.Its timing, however, remains uncertain, with a section of lawmakers being of the view that Parliament can be summoned after Independence Day to debate it.The ongoing monsoon session is scheduled to end on Aug 13, leaving the government with not much time to pursue its ambitious agenda that seeks to raise Lok Sabha’s maximum strength from the existing 550 to 850.Sukhbir demanded implementation of one-third reservation for women in Lok Sabha and state assemblies. He said, “SAD also demanded a fair and equitable delimitation.” Incidentally, his wife had made a fiery speech against a similar bill last time, flaying the government for linking reservation for women to delimitation.The changed political environment and the fact that the government may write into the new bill all the assurances it has made verbally may have persuaded his party and DMK to consider a rethink.NCP MP Supriya Sule had earlier suggested that if the bill proposes a rise in Lok Sabha seats of every state by an equal proportion, it would not create any problem, though she had added that they will be part of opposition consultations before making a final decision.
Article Summary: Government likely to bring back delimitation bill, but timing not clear yet. Akali Dal president Sukhbir Singh Badal reversed his party's earlier opposition to the rollout of the women's reservation law from 2029 with an increase in the Lok Sabha's strength by 50%. He also supported any fresh move to implement the two together.

Article Title: Restore J&K statehood, says human rights forum
Article Text:
The forum also backed statehood for Ladakh and its inclusion in the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution.

SRINAGAR: The Forum for Human Rights in J&K has called for full restoration of statehood and repeal of 2019 Reorganisation Act, cautioning that linking statehood to the security situation and terrorist attacks could erode democratic rights in the Union territory.It presented its annual report “Seven Years Under Union Rule — With a Special Section on Ladakh & Pakistan-held Territories of J&K (Aug 2025–July 2026)” to National Conference president Farooq Abdullah, PDP president and former J&K CM Mehbooba Mufti, CPM’s MY Tarigami and Congress’s J&K president Tariq Hamid Karra.The forum said arguments that restoration of statehood is “not appropriate” because of security concerns and terrorist attacks are dangerous and could be used to undermine people’s democratic rights.It also backed statehood for Ladakh and its inclusion in the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution.It praised J&K HC for a series of orders quashing detentions under Public Safety Act and granting bail under UAPA and PSA “…but we are constrained to note that its repeated strictures do not appear to have led to course correction by police,” the report said.The forum, an informal group of concerned citizens, is co-chaired by former Union home secretary Gopal Pillai and Radha Kumar, a former member of the group of interlocutors for J&K. The report also alleged a familiar backlash against Kashmiris after terrorist attacks, including the recent Red Fort blast in New Delhi, saying they faced housing discrimination, forced evictions, aggressive verification and hostility from neighbours, shopkeepers, and co-workers.
Article Summary: The Forum for Human Rights in J&K has called for full restoration of statehood and repeal of 2019 Reorganisation Act. The forum also backed statehood for Ladakh and its inclusion in the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution. It presented its annual report “Seven Years Under Union Rule — With a Special Section on Ladakh & Pakistan-held Territories of J &K (Aug 2025–July 2026)” to National Conference president Farooq Abdullah.

This is the addiction of the 21st century, and then you are told to work for Blinkit or Uber, or to do manual labour. You can indulge in this 21st-century addiction, but you cannot get a job; you cannot find employment in this country," Rahul said.He also criticised the government's economic policies, arguing that demonetisation and what he called "wrong GST" had damaged India's manufacturing sector."The first door is manufacturing. Small businessmen who used to provide employment, and industries like leather, textile, and automobile that used to manufacture in India... all that has been finished. The first door is closed," he added.Meanwhile, in Jharkhand, the state government held talks with several student groups amid protests over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations but failed to break the deadlock, with the protesting aspirants deciding to continue their agitation until their demands are met.A five-member government panel, comprising state ministers, first met a faction of protesters led by JLKM leader Devendra Nath Mahto, whose hunger strike over the issue entered its seventh day. The panel then separately met delegations of the Congress-backed NSUI, Adivasi Chhatra Sangh (ACS) and Jharkhand Chhatra Morcha (JCM).On Friday night, the government had held similar talks with a delegation of the JPSC/JSSC Reforms Manch.The ruling JMM's student wing, JCM, placed five demands before the panel, including cancellation of the 14th Jharkhand PSC Civil Services Examination.The NSUI submitted six demands, including a CID probe into all JPSC and JSSC examinations under suspicion within 90 days and the establishment of a Jharkhand Testing Agency (JTA) on the lines of the National Testing Agency, its spokesperson Sanjiv Shah said.Another round of talks between the government and the students is scheduled for Sunday.
Article Summary: Kiren Rijiju takes a dig at Rahul Gandhi over 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' programme in Uttar Pradesh's Prayagraj. He says Gandhi should have travelled to Ranchi, where students are protesting over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations.

Article Title: Supriya Sule opposes FCRA Bill, urges Centre to withdraw it or send it to JPC
Article Text:
Supriya Sule said foreign funding should not automatically be treated with suspicion

‘ Foreign funding cannot always be viewed with suspicion’

Sule backs youth protests, questions party symbol decisions

NEW DELHI: NCP (SP) working president Supriya Sule on Saturday opposed the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 in its present form, urging the Centre either to withdraw the proposed legislation or refer it to a Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) for wider discussion.Sule, the Lok Sabha MP from Baramati, said all political parties should be given an opportunity to examine the contentious legislation before Parliament takes it up for consideration. She cautioned the government against rushing the bill through Parliament, amid reports that it could be discussed and passed next week.“We reject and disagree with the present form of the FCRA bill. If the government is not ready to withdraw the bill, then it should send it to a JPC. In a strong democracy, merely opposing something is not enough; we also have to sit together and discuss it,” she said.The proposed legislation seeks to establish a designated authority for the vesting, supervision, management and disposal of foreign contributions and assets in cases involving cancellation, surrender or expiry of an organisation’s FCRA registration.The bill also provides for provisional and permanent vesting of such assets.Critics have argued that the proposed changes could give the government greater control over organisations receiving foreign contributions.Sule said foreign funding should not automatically be treated with suspicion, arguing that overseas contributions can support legitimate work in areas such as healthcare and education.She said action should be taken if foreign funds are linked to illegal activities such as drug trafficking or terrorism, but questioned the rationale for viewing every foreign-funded organisation negatively.“There are organisations such as the Gates Foundation and USAID that have been doing good work for many years. Why should we look at every foreign-funded organisation with a bad eye?” she said.She also compared foreign funding with money sent home by Indians living abroad, arguing that the source of money alone should not determine whether it is viewed negatively.According to official figures, 13,520 entities received foreign remittances totalling Rs 55,741 crore between 2019 and 2022.As of July 15, 2026, there were 14,449 active FCRA registrations, while 22,498 registrations had been cancelled and 15,212 had expired.The FCRA regulates the receipt and utilisation of foreign contributions by NGOs, charitable institutions, educational bodies, religious trusts and other organisations.Sule also commented on the ongoing protests by students, saying young people should not face such treatment while seeking education.“What happened at Jantar Mantar should not happen anywhere in the country. Our children want to study and this is happening to them. I read that ministers from Jharkhand have ordered an inquiry into it,” she said.She also backed Uddhav Thackeray in the dispute over the Shiv Sena's name and election symbol, arguing that party organisations and constitutions should be considered while deciding control of political parties.On the NCP dispute, Sule said the legal battle remained unresolved and alleged that her party had been waiting for a hearing.“Sharad Pawar is the founder president of the NCP and injustice has been done to him. We have been asking for a date for a long time, but why are we not getting a date?” she said.Sule also criticised the Maharashtra government's approach to farm loan waivers and called for political criticism to remain focused on issues rather than becoming personal.On the proposed delimitation legislation, Sule said it would be premature to comment before the bill was introduced. She added that the NCP (SP) would discuss the legislation with its alliance partners once it came before Parliament.Sule further said Prime Minister Narendra Modi had agreed to meet NCP (SP) MPs on Monday to discuss issues concerning their constituencies, amid the opposition's contention that Parliament was not functioning properly.
Article Summary: Supriya Sule opposes the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 in its present form. She urged the Centre either to withdraw the proposed legislation or refer it to a Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) for wider discussion. Sule said foreign funding should not automatically be treated with suspicion.

Article Title: 'We stand in solidarity': CJP delegation reaches Ranchi to support students protesting JPSC, JSSC exams
Article Text:
Ranchi: Demonstrators holding posters during an indefinite hunger strike as part of a protest against the Jharkhand government over alleged irregularities in the 14th JPSC examination, JSSC-CGL and other recruitment tests, demanding a CBI probe and reforms in the recruitment agencies, in Ranchi, Jharkhand. 'We fully support the students'

Students demand cancellation, CBI probe

A delegation of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) arrived in Ranchi on Saturday to extend support to students protesting alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations conducted by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC).CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka said the party stood in “complete solidarity” with the protesting students and would provide them with all forms of support.“CJP stands in complete solidarity with the students of Jharkhand,” Ranka said in a post on X.He added that the delegation was travelling under the leadership of Mukallrounder and Akshay Shinde and would support the students during their ongoing agitation.Speaking to PTI, CJP national coordinator Mukesh said the party fully supports students protesting over alleged irregularities in JPSC and JSSC examinations and repeated paper leaks. “We stand with the students and will continue to support them,” he said, adding that the party would share its experience from the Jantar Mantar movement with the protesting students.“Our support may not be from the stage, but we are standing with them,” Mukesh said, asserting that the CJP would continue backing the students until there is transparency in recruitment examinations and paper leaks are stopped.“Till when will this continue to happen?” he asked.The protests in Jharkhand have intensified following allegations of irregularities in recruitment examinations. Students have been demanding the cancellation of the 14th JPSC Combined Civil Services Preliminary Examination, a CBI probe into alleged irregularities in JPSC and JSSC-CGL examinations, and the release of OMR sheets and answer scripts.Student leader Devendra Nath Mahto has also been observing an indefinite hunger strike over the issue. On Wednesday, the fourth day of his fast, Mahto consumed water after climate activist Sonam Wangchuk urged him to do so during a video call, while maintaining that his agitation would continue until the government responds to the students’ demands.The Jharkhand government has said it is examining the allegations. CM Hemant Soren recently met Governor Santosh Kumar Gangwar and said the government would “soon take action” on the matter.
Article Summary: A delegation of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) arrived in Ranchi on Saturday to extend support to students protesting alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations. CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka said the party stood in “complete solidarity” with the protesting students and would provide them with all forms of support.

Article Title: 'Which freedom fighter received most severe punishment?' Kerala orders probe into Savarkar quiz
Article Text:
File photo: Vinayak Damodar Savarkar

Education department says quiz was not authorised

Pinarayi Vijayan accuses government of 'colluding' with RSS

Left groups, IUML leaders criticise question

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A political row has erupted in Kerala over a school quiz question that described Hindutva ideologue Vinayak Damodar Savarkar as the freedom fighter who received the "most severe punishment" from the British, prompting general education minister N Samsudheen to order an inquiry.The "Freedom Quiz" was conducted on August 6 for lower primary students in schools in the Kasaragod, Kumbla and Manjeshwar sub-districts, according to news agency PTI.The disputed question asked: "Who is the freedom fighter that received the most severe punishment from the British?" Savarkar was given as the answer.The minister's office said Samsudheen has directed the director of general education to establish who prepared and conducted the quiz and take stringent action against those responsible.According to the minister's office, the quiz was not included in the activity calendar of either the Social Science Club or the General Education Department. Neither had authorised anyone to independently prepare the questions or conduct the competition."The person who included the historically incorrect question holds a prejudiced view," the minister's office said, adding that the Education Director had been instructed to identify those responsible and take strict action.As per PTI, teachers associated with the Social Science Club had prepared the questionnaire.The controversy has since drawn criticism from the CPI(M) and Left-affiliated student and youth organisations, which accused the Congress-led UDF government of allowing what they described as a "Sangh Parivar agenda" to enter the education system.CPI(M) veteran and former Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan accused the UDF government of "colluding" with the RSS and alleged that efforts were being made to conceal Savarkar's history and glorify him.Addressing a press conference in Kannur, Vijayan alleged that the Centre and the RSS were attempting to "rewrite history". He also linked the controversy to the Centre's efforts to implement its new education policy in Kerala.Former general education minister V Sivankutty also criticised the question, alleging that it was part of an attempt to "saffronise" Kerala's general education sector and distort the history of India's freedom struggle.Sivankutty demanded a comprehensive inquiry, strict action against those responsible and the withdrawal of the disputed question and answer. He also sought an apology from the General Education Department.SFI state secretary P S Sanjeev alleged that the quiz sought to portray Savarkar as a freedom fighter. In a social media post, he criticised the UDF government and alleged that the general education portfolio was being used to create space for the Sangh Parivar.DYFI state secretary K Sanoj also criticised the government, saying there was no justification for a school quiz to contain a question that allegedly glorified Savarkar.Senior Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) leader and former minister M K Muneer said portraying Savarkar as a patriot was part of the RSS-BJP agenda.Muneer, however, said that if the question had indeed been included in the quiz, the matter should be seriously examined and those responsible identified, adding that it should not be treated lightly.
Article Summary: "Freedom Quiz" conducted on August 6 for lower primary students in schools in Kasaragod, Kumbla and Manjeshwar sub-districts. Question asked: "Who is the freedom fighter that received the most severe punishment from the British?" Savarkar was given as the answer. Education department says quiz was not authorised.

NEW DELHI: Arunachal Pradesh chief minister Pema Khandu on Saturday rejected reports of Chinese military encroachment in the state and said that the Army was effectively patrolling and safeguarding the territory.Speaking to reporters, Khandu said, "No signs of encroachment in Arunachal Pradesh; Indian Army effectively patrolling and safeguarding the territory."Khandu's remarks came a day after the Centre identified 27 locations in Arunachal Pradesh by their standard names on the official map of the country, amid China's repeated attempts to rename places in the border state.The government said the exercise was aimed at ensuring the correct identification of the locations and improving public awareness of their geographical and historical significance."Identifying them formally on the Survey of India map of Arunachal Pradesh is aimed at facilitating their accurate recognition and better awareness among the public at large," an official statement said.New Delhi has consistently rejected Beijing's practice of assigning Chinese names to places in Arunachal Pradesh, calling the move "vain and preposterous".India has maintained that such actions do not alter the "undeniable" fact that Arunachal Pradesh "was, is, and will" remain an integral part of the country.Several of the locations newly marked on the official map hold strategic importance because of their proximity to the Line of Actual Control (LAC) and their role in past India-China military confrontations.Among them is Long Ju, one of the earliest flashpoints between the two countries. Chinese troops entered the area in 1959, three years before the 1962 India-China war.The official map also includes Maja village in Upper Subansiri district near Long Ju, Bisa village and the strategically significant mountain passes of Dzo La, Riza La and Pukur La.Another key location is Thag La, the high-altitude pass where one of the opening battles of the 1962 India-China war took place.Jairampur in Changlang district has also been formally identified. The town serves as an important logistics hub for the movement of security forces towards eastern Arunachal Pradesh and the Myanmar border.Other locations added to the map include the high-altitude lake Sambho Sarovar, Bara Kundun, Chhota Kundun, Dhan Bari, Pritnagar, Teritnagar, Ramnagar, Jaswant Garh, Sagar, Padma, Jyotinagar, Baisakhi, Sher-e-Thapa Memorial, Chhota Ropuk, Bara Ropuk, Shivaji Nagar, Sunpura, Kamlang Nagar and Buddhamandir.India has repeatedly dismissed China's attempts to assign what it calls "fictitious names" to places in Arunachal Pradesh, saying such efforts seek to create "baseless narratives" and cannot alter the "undeniable" reality on the ground. It followed this with a second list covering 15 locations in 2021 and another naming 11 places in 2023. Beijing uses the term Zangnan to refer to Arunachal Pradesh, a claim India has consistently rejected.

NEW DELHI: A 17-year-old girl died while being taken to hospital in Jammu and Kashmir's Rajouri district after the vehicle carrying her remained stuck in mud for nearly three hours. The district administration has suspended a government engineer and ordered an inquiry into the incident.The girl, a resident of remote Methyani village, had fallen seriously ill on Friday and was being taken to Government Medical College (GMC), Rajouri, when the vehicle became stranded following a mudslide at Chak Methyani, officials told news agency PTI.Volunteers later managed to pull the vehicle out, but the girl's condition deteriorated and she died while she was being taken to the hospital, according to officials.The incident occurred on the Chak Methyani-Panglar-Kotecharwal road, which serves as the only road link for several remote villages in the area. The road was washed away near Methyani during last year's monsoon and had subsequently been restored temporarily.The same stretch was hit by another mudslide around two weeks ago, leaving the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) road unmotorable, officials said.According to the report submitted by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (ADC), Kotranka, the girl had been suffering from an illness for nearly a month and had previously been admitted to Government Medical College Hospital, Jammu. She was discharged around two weeks ago, but her condition worsened again, prompting her family to take her to GMC Rajouri.The ADC's report said the blocked road resulted in a delay of nearly two to three hours. It also found that the stretch remained in "extremely poor condition" due to landslides and deep ditches, making it unfit for vehicular movement.The report further noted that residents of Narla Bamble, Kotecharwal and Panglar continued to face difficulties in transporting patients, food grains and fertilisers.The district administration said the executive engineer, PMGSY division Rajouri, had informed officials through an official WhatsApp group that the road had been restored and was "trafficable". However, subsequent verification by the ADC found otherwise.Taking note of the report, district development commissioner (DDC) Rajouri Abhishek Sharma ordered the immediate suspension of the assistant executive engineer (AEE), PMGSY Sub-Division Kalakote, who was in charge of the road project, pending an inquiry.The DDC said the failure to restore the road despite repeated directions indicated "prima facie negligence and non-compliance with official instructions".The executive engineer has also been asked to explain why disciplinary proceedings should not be initiated against him for allegedly misreporting the road's status and failing to ensure its timely restoration. His salary has been withheld pending consideration of his explanation.The additional district development commissioner (ADDC), Rajouri, has been directed to conduct a detailed inquiry and submit a comprehensive report within seven days.
Article Summary: A 17-year-old girl died while being taken to hospital in J-K's Rajouri district. The vehicle carrying her remained stuck in mud for nearly three hours. The district administration has suspended a government engineer and ordered an inquiry into the incident.

NEW DELHI: The Union ministry of tribal affairs on Thursday told the Lok Sabha that it has received several representations raising concerns over the displacement of people due to the Ken-Betwa river-link project in Madhya Pradesh.The ministry said it has forwarded the representations to the state government and the concerned district administrations for examination and appropriate action.In a written reply to questions from Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and Samajwadi Party MP Ajendra Singh Lodhi on the rehabilitation of tribal families affected by the project, compliance with the Forest Rights Act (FRA), and alleged evictions, the ministry said it had not received any complaints specifically claiming that compensation disbursed under the project had failed to reach beneficiaries.The ministry, however, said it had received representations "raising issues of displacement" due to the project.It added that the representations had been forwarded to the Madhya Pradesh government and the concerned district administrations for examination and appropriate action, while noting that the implementation of the Forest Rights Act (FRA) rests with state governments and Union Territory administrations.Minister of state for tribal affairs Durgadas Uikey, in his written reply, said the representations had been referred to the state authorities.
