We told him about the irregularities in exams here. We told him that Congress is in the government in Jharkhand and they should help us. He told us that he stands with students," Paswan said.According to JPSC JSSC Reform Manch, protesting students have finalised an 11-member delegation for talks with the state government. The group comprises eight student representatives, one lawyer and two technical experts.The eight student representatives are Piyush Kumar Singh, Ravindra Paswan, Rajesh Prasad, Neetu Kujur, Kartik Soren, Ravindra, Ankit Kumar and Shalu Singh.Students have also demanded that any dialogue with the government be held in the presence of the media.Ranchi Sadar SDO Rajat Kumar and ADM Dhananjay Kumar reached Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium to hear the grievances of the protesting aspirants."We came to speak with our younger brothers about how we can assist them in their preparations for the future," Rajat Kumar said.A protester said there had been a suggestion that a four- or five-member delegation should participate in talks, but students insisted on a transparent process.Amid the continuing agitation, students announced a "Vidhan Sabha Gherao" on August 10 if their demands are not met. Protester Radhe Kumar said the decision was taken after the government initiated contact with the students.JMM MLA Jairam Kumar Mahato urged the government to immediately open talks, warning that "something untoward will happen" if the situation remains unresolved.Activist Sonam Wangchuk rejected reports that student leader Devendra Nath Mahato had ended his hunger strike after speaking with him. A total of six demonstrators are presently on a hunger strike.In a video message on X, Wangchuk said, "He consumed water, not food; I want to clarify this."He added, "He was fasting without water and without food, which is, in a way, like suicide. So, I only urged him to consume water and salt now and continue his fast."Mahato began his indefinite hunger strike on August 2 at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium. He is now continuing the fast on water and salt.Jharkhand minister Shilpi Neha Tirkey said on Thursday that the government was investigating the allegations and that 19 people had been arrested.
Article Summary: Protest by JPSC and JSSC aspirants in Jharkhand entered its 14th day on Thursday. Students demanding action over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations. Political pressure on the Hemant Soren government intensified. 11-member delegation finalised for talks with the state government.

Article Title: Any post against PM Modi to be deleted in three hours: Arvind Kejriwal on new social media law
Article Text:
Kejriwal slams Centre's new social media law

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Aam Aadmi Party supremo Arvind Kejriwal on Friday launched a sharp attack on the Centre over its newly introduced social media law, alleging that it is aimed at silencing criticism of the government and reflects Prime Minister Narendra Modi's growing fear of public protests.Addressing supporters, former Delhi CM Kejriwal claimed the new law would require social media platforms to take down any post flagged by the government within three hours."The Modi government has introduced a new law. If the government asks any social media platform, whether Instagram, Facebook or any other platform, to delete a post or video, it will have to be removed within three hours," he said.He alleged that the provision would be used to target posts critical of the government on issues such as paper leaks, the ethanol policy and corruption, while allowing abusive content from its supporters to remain online."If you speak against Modi ji, the government, paper leaks, the ethanol issue or corruption, your post will be deleted within three hours. But if people associated with them use abusive language or target women, no action is taken against such content," he alleged.AAP chief Kejriwal further claimed that Prime Minister Modi has become increasingly anxious after recent youth-led protests and demonstrations at Jantar Mantar."Modi ji fears the people of this country. He fears the youth, children and women. Ever since the protests at Jantar Mantar, he has been gripped by fear," Kejriwal alleged.Arguing that censorship cannot substitute governance, the former Delhi chief minister said silencing criticism would only deepen public resentment."The solution is not to silence people's voices. If the government does good work, people will praise it on their own. The public has no personal enmity with anyone. But if you suppress criticism instead of addressing people's concerns, public anger will only grow," he said.Kejriwal also warned that governments that fear their own citizens eventually lose public support."The days of a ruler who fears his own people are numbered. The more you try to suppress the voices of the people, the stronger their anger will become," he said.Earlier to this, Kejriwal also claimed that Meta restricted his account and slammed Mark Zuckerberg-led social media giant.
Article Summary: Aam Aadmi Party supremo Arvind Kejriwal slams Centre's new social media law. Former Delhi CM claims the new law would require social media platforms to take down any post flagged by the government within three hours. He alleges that the provision would be used to target posts critical of the government on issues such as paper leaks, the ethanol policy and corruption.

Article Title: "I am willing to defend": Candace Owens ignites fresh Charlie Kirk murder controversy with bold Tyler Robinson 'patsy' claim
Article Text:
Candace Owens (Image via Getty)

Candace Owens stands by Tyler Robinson "patsy" claim

“All evening the Candace Owens people have been saying she makes no claims so she doesn’t have to defend any.

They claim I said there was overwhelming evidence for the prosecution of Robinson which is true I said that so I meed to defend it.”

“However, Candace did make a reverse claim. She said there is overwhelming evidence Robinson was set up by the feds as a patsy. So I will take the position that the evidence is more compelling that Tyler was a lone shooter not set up by the feds. She takes the position of her claim, which she says has overwhelming evidence he was a patsy put there by the feds.

If she agrees, then we are all set.”

"Geez, he is still going. Yes, Andrew. I firmly believe there is evidence Tyler Robinson was set up as a patsy and I am more than happy to defend that claim. Can we now take this offline and organize the debate officially. This is just getting exhausting, which I think is your intention. Yes or no? We aren’t doing this all day again.”

Andrew Wilson and Candace Owens move closer to a public debate

“And to be extra clear—- yes, yes, yes I accept the claim there is more evidence Tyler Robinson was set up as a patsy than evidence that he committed this crime. I am willing to defend, gladly, with the facts of the case presented thus far.”

$300,000

Candace Owens and political commentator Andrew Wilson have taken their disagreement over the Charlie Kirk murder case into public view, turning a debate invitation into a heated exchange on social media. At the center of the dispute is Tyler Robinson, the suspect in the case. Owens has firmly defended her belief that Robinson was framed, while Wilson insists she should publicly defend that position in a formal debate.The disagreement escalated after Wilson argued that Owens had already made a clear claim about the case and should be prepared to defend it publicly.He wrote:Wilson continued:Owens responded by making it clear that she had no intention of backing away from her position.Owens reinforced her stance with another message, removing any doubt about where she stands.The exchange has intensified interest in a potential public debate between the two commentators. Reports indicate that Wilson has claimed he offered Owensto participate, adding even more attention to the ongoing dispute.The discussion comes as the Charlie Kirk murder case continues to generate widespread public interest and online debate. While Owens argues that the available evidence points toward Robinson being framed, Wilson maintains that the evidence more strongly supports the conclusion that Robinson acted alone.At this stage, neither side has changed its position. Instead, both appear willing to defend their respective arguments in a formal debate if arrangements are finalized.Until that happens, the social media exchange has become another high-profile chapter in the wider discussion surrounding one of the most closely watched criminal cases in recent months. As attention remains fixed on the legal proceedings, the proposed Owens-Wilson debate has emerged as a separate flashpoint, drawing supporters and critics from both sides while keeping the controversy firmly in the public spotlight.
Article Summary: Candace Owens and political commentator Andrew Wilson have taken their disagreement over the Charlie Kirk murder case into public view, turning a debate invitation into a heated exchange on social media. At the center of the dispute is Tyler Robinson, the suspect in the case. Owens has firmly defended her belief that Robinson was framed, while Wilson insists she should publicly defend that position.

Article Title: Jude Bellingham’s girlfriend Ashlyn Castro’s ‘desperate’ family struggle revealed as police footage resurfaces: ‘I’ve just been attacked’
Article Text:
Jude Bellingham’s girlfriend Ashlyn Castro’s ‘desperate’ family struggle revealed as police footage resurfaces: ‘I’ve just been attacked’ (Image via Henderson Police)

Jude Bellingham's girlfriend Ashlyn Castro describes alleged attack by mother Tina

Jude Bellingham relationship brings family dispute into spotlight

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jude Bellingham’s girlfriend Ashlyn Castro is facing renewed attention after police bodycam footage from a 2024 family incident showed her describing an alleged attack by her mother, Tina. The footage, obtained by The Mail on Sunday, shows Castro crying as she tells an officer, “I’ve just been attacked by my mom.” The incident happened in a hotel car park in Henderson, Nevada, when Castro was trying to help her mother find a place to stay. The report also details a long-running family struggle that Castro has spoken about publicly, including her mother’s mental health problems.According to The Mail on Sunday, Castro was trying to take her mother back to California in July 2024 when the situation turned violent. Castro told police that she had booked a hotel room for Tina but later realised she had chosen the wrong hotel.She said her mother then attacked her.“She pulled my hair down and started punching my face,” Castro told the officer while struggling to control her emotions.Tina was questioned separately by police and denied attacking her daughter. “She hates me for some reason, I never did anything to her,” she said.Police later arrested Tina after seeing a video Castro had taken and noticing scratches on her hands and a swollen lip. Tina protested, saying, “A busted lip? I never touched her lip!”Castro later gave police a written statement saying: “I was trying to get my mother a hotel room when she started attacking me, pulling my hair, punching me, scratching me.She didn’t think I was getting her the room so she attacked me.”The report says Tina was fined $200 for domestic battery. It also says she is now wanted for contempt of court after failing to pay the fine.Castro’s relationship with Jude Bellingham became public months after the incident. The couple have since been seen together at major events, including during England’s 2026 World Cup campaign. Castro regularly supported the Real Madrid midfielder from the stands and was also seen with Bellingham’s mother, Denise.The family dispute later became public when Tina mentioned Bellingham on TikTok while speaking about her daughter. “Who is this Jude Bellingham?” she said. “You disobeyed your mum, lied about her, left her in shelters.”Castro has previously spoken about the impact of her mother’s illness and her decision to discuss mental health publicly. “This is extremely personal. This is my real life. I lost my father a few years ago,” she said.“My mum is mentally ill… moving forward, I will talk about things that are important such as mental health. This is something that I wanted to use my platform for but I just wasn’t ready.”She has also said she wants to start a charity supporting people dealing with mental health issues and their families.The Mail on Sunday report also spoke to Castro’s brother Trever, who described the family’s past as traumatic. He said their parents had serious personal struggles and that the family had been affected by them for years.Despite the public family conflict, Castro has continued to build her own career as a model and influencer while maintaining her relationship with Bellingham.
Article Summary: Jude Bellingham’s girlfriend Ashlyn Castro describes alleged attack by mother Tina. Castro was trying to take her mother back to California in July 2024 when the situation turned violent. Castro told police that she had booked a hotel room for Tina but later realised she had chosen the wrong hotel. She said her mother then attacked her.

Article Title: 4.3-magnitude earthquake jolts Nashik; tremors trigger cracks in houses
Article Text:
According to the National Centre for Seismology (NCS), the earthquake occurred at around 10 pm on Saturday, while the 3.3-magnitude tremor was recorded at 5.33 am on Sunday.

(With agency inputs)





NASHIK: A mild earthquake followed by tremors hit Maharashtra's Nashik, causing cracks in houses in some areas of the district, officials said on Sunday.There was no report of any loss of life, they said.An earthquake of 4.3 magnitude struck Nashik at 10 pm on Saturday, followed by a tremor of 3.3 magnitude at 5.33 am on Sunday, as per the National Centre for Seismology (NCS).A 4.3-magnitude earthquake followed by a 3.3-magnitude tremor struck Maharashtra’s Nashik district, causing cracks in some houses, officials said on Sunday.No casualties or loss of life have been reported so far, they said.According to the National Centre for Seismology (NCS), the earthquake occurred at around 10 pm on Saturday, while the 3.3-magnitude tremor was recorded at 5.33 am on Sunday.The seismic activity was recorded at a depth of 5 km in the Bhanwad area, near the Hatgad mountain range along the Maharashtra-Gujarat border, officials said.Tremors were felt in several parts of Nashik district, including Nashik city, Surgana, Kalwan, Deola, Chandwad, Peth, Dindori and Niphad talukas, triggering panic among residents, many of whom rushed out of their homes.Cracks were reported in the walls of houses in Bhadar village in Surgana taluka and Nanashi village in Dindori taluka, district administration officials said.No casualties were reported. Officials also inspected dams in the affected areas and found no damage, they said."People should not fear. They should not believe any rumours. However, everyone should remain alert and take safety precautions," district Collector Ayush Prasad told PTI.Earlier, tremors were recorded in the district from July 25 to 28 and also on August 6.
Article Summary: An earthquake of 4.3 magnitude struck Nashik at 10 pm on Saturday. It was followed by a tremor of 3.3-magnitude at 5.33 am on Sunday. No casualties or loss of life have been reported so far, officials said.

Article Title: ‘Married 25 women using fake IDs’: BJP MLA alleges he was duped into marrying his daughter to conman
Article Text:
Tiwari alleged that Prakhar had duped several women across different states, including Maharashtra, of crores of rupees by allegedly luring them into relationships while using fake identities.

(With agency inputs)





SSITAPUR: Uttar Pradesh BJP MLA from Sevata Gyan Tiwari has lodged a complaint alleging that his daughter was duped into marrying a conman who had allegedly married around 25 women using fake identities and cheated them.Following the complaint, police registered an FIR, officials said on Sunday.According to news agency PTI, police have arrested Anuj Trivedi and his son Prakhar Trivedi in connection with the case, based on the complaint filed by the MLA. Tiwari also levelled the allegations in a social media video posted on August 6, in which he appeared alongside his daughter.According to the complaint lodged at Reusa police station, Tiwari’s daughter Pragya married Prakhar Trivedi, son of Anuj Trivedi and a resident of Chandrawal in Mishrikh, in 2024.The MLA alleged that before the marriage, Anuj Trivedi had portrayed himself as a prominent real estate businessman based in Mumbai and concealed his alleged criminal history and previous cases.The complaint stated that the marriage was finalised after local inquiries and favourable feedback from people regarded as influential in the area.However, around two-and-a-half years after the marriage, the family came across information on social media and through other sources about Prakhar Trivedi’s alleged activities.Tiwari alleged that Prakhar had duped several women across different states, including Maharashtra, of crores of rupees by allegedly luring them into relationships while using fake identities. He further alleged that Prakhar had been involved in around 25 marriages.The MLA said he had severed all social and personal ties with the accused family and brought his daughter back home. He alleged that the episode had caused deep trauma to his family and affected his social standing as a public representative.Following Tiwari’s complaint, Reusa police registered a case against Anuj Trivedi on charges of cheating and initiated legal proceedings, officials said.In a social media video, Tiwari alleged that his family had been cheated and demanded strict punishment for Anuj Trivedi, including the death penalty. He also said that if his son-in-law was found guilty, he should be dealt with severely under the law.
Article Summary: Uttar Pradesh BJP MLA from Sevata Gyan Tiwari has lodged a complaint alleging that his daughter was duped into marrying a conman. Prakhar Trivedi had allegedly married around 25 women using fake identities and cheated them.

Article Title: Woman crushed between vehicles after smash-up in Delhi; kin alleges Mercedes driver was speeding, drunk
Article Text:
The smash-up happened around 8 am on the narrow road in front of Gate No. 1 of Himalaya Apartment in Mamurpur.

Narela crash: Both vehicles damaged, Merc driver held





NEW DELHI: A 70-year-old woman who was feeding birds and insects on the roadside Saturday morning was killed when a head-on crash between a Mercedes-Benz and a WagonR sent the smaller car into a parked three-wheeler, trapping her between the vehicles in Narela, Outer Delhi.Urmila Bhardwaj, a resident of Mamurpur village, was crushed between the WagonR and the parked vehicle, a goods carrier.Police arrested the Mercedes driver, 27-year-old Subham Sharma, the son of a Haryana Police sub-inspector.Urmila’s family alleged Sharma was speeding and drunk. Police have seized an empty liquor bottle and a beer bottle from his car.The beer bottle was visible in a video shot by local residents after the crash.A senior police officer said Subham was returning home from a party with friends. “We have sent his blood for examination and the report will confirm whether he was drunk or not,” the officer said.Police said Subham had completed his MA and was unemployed. “The car belonged to him and was purchased from a friend, although its ownership has not been transferred to his name,” the officer said.The smash-up happened around 8 am on the narrow road in front of Gate No.1 of Himalaya Apartment in Mamurpur.The case was registered on the complaint of Geeta Verma, the wife of WagonR driver Narendra Kumar. Geeta told police that she, her husband and their 3-year-old child were going to Lajpat Rai market.The Mercedes, which was speeding and driven rashly, smashed into their WagonR head-on, pushing backwards their car that crashed into a three-wheeler parked near a wall. Urmila, who was standing near the three-wheeler, was caught in between. The public took her to a hospital, where she was declared dead.Geeta and Narendra also sustained minor injuries.Locals caught Subham and handed him over to police. The Mercedes sustained extensive damage to its front, with its airbags deployed, while the other vehicle was also badly damaged.Sunil, a relative of Urmila, said “My aunt was injured after the Mercedes, which was being driven at high speed, hit another vehicle. The driver was drunk. I took her to the hospital, where she was declared dead,” he said.A local resident and eyewitness, Sandhya, also alleged that the Mercedes was being driven at high speed and that the driver appeared to lose control before hitting other vehicles.A case has been registered under sections 281 (rash driving), 285 (danger or obstruction in public way or line of navigation) and 106(1) (causing death by negligence) of BNS.
Article Summary: A head-on crash between a Mercedes-Benz and a WagonR sent the smaller car into a parked three-wheeler, trapping her between the vehicles in Narela, Outer Delhi. Urmila Bhardwaj, a resident of Mamurpur village, was crushed between the Wagon R and the parked vehicle. Police arrested the Mercedes driver, 27-year-old Subham Sharma, the son of a Haryana Police sub-inspector.Urmila’s family alleged Sharma was speeding and drunk.

Article Title: Bike at foothills, phone location elsewhere: Bengaluru techie goes missing on solo trek
Article Text:
Advait went missing after setting out on a solo trek to Shivagange Hill (Photo credit: Incredible India) in Bengaluru Rural district.





BENGALURU: A city techie went missing after setting out on a solo trek to Shivagange Hill near Dobbaspet in Bengaluru Rural district Friday morning, triggering a multi-agency search across the treacherous terrain.His last known sighting was captured on CCTV as he parked his bike at the foothills before starting the ascent.Advait Upadhyay, 31, from Kadugodi in east Bengaluru and son of an Indore-based businessman, told his fiancée Prapti Chauhan he was heading for the trek around 7.30am. She filed a missing person’s complaint in the evening, following which police found the bike, but his mobile phone was switched off.Advait had reportedly rented a motorbike from Whitefield five days ago. “The rented motorcycle was found parked near the base of the hill, but we have not found any further clue so far,” a police officer involved in the search told TOI.Police said his mobile phone’s last known location was traced to an area that does not fall along the trekking route, deepening the mystery over his whereabouts.Located about 50km from Bengaluru, Shivagange rises to 4,488 feet above sea level and is a popular trekking destination.The climb is moderately challenging, with steep stretches and narrow, rock-cut steps.Following the complaint, police teams rushed to Shivagange and launched an intensive search. Police personnel, assisted by drones and search-and-rescue teams, spent more than six hours scouring dense vegetation and steep, rocky terrain.Teams have been concentrating on the area around Shantala Drop, a dangerous cliff point atop the hill.
Article Summary: Advait Upadhyay, 31, told his fiancée Prapti Chauhan he was heading for the trek around 7.30am. His last known sighting was captured on CCTV as he parked his bike at the foothills. Police found the bike, but his mobile phone was switched off.

Article Title: No weekly offs, leave and workplace harassment: Mysuru woman dies by suicide, accuses manager
Article Text:
Nageshwari, 42, worked as a product promoter at a shopping mall.





MYSURU: A 42-year-old woman working as a product promoter at a shopping mall in west Mysuru allegedly died by suicide on Friday, accusing her manager of harassment.Vijayanagar police have booked the manager of a marketing agency on charges of abetment of suicide under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).Nageshwari, a resident of Hinkal, left behind a suicide note in which she alleged that her manager, Dolly, who monitored her work from Bengaluru, harassed her by forcing her to admit to a mistake committed by someone else.She also claimed that Dolly continued to torment her by threatening to replace her with another employee and pressured her to resign from her job.Nageshwari, who had been working with the marketing agency for the past three years, further alleged that she was not given a weekly off after Dolly became her manager and was also denied leave.Her husband told police that about a month ago, his wife began complaining about Dolly's behaviour. He said that while he was away from home, she consumed a poisonous substance. Although she was rushed to a hospital, she succumbed late on Friday.Police said a case has been registered and an investigation is underway.
Article Summary: Nageshwari, a resident of Hinkal, left behind a suicide note. She alleged that her manager, Dolly, monitored her work from Bengaluru. She also claimed that Dolly continued to torment her by threatening to replace her with another employee.

Article Title: Strait of Hormuz standoff: What conditions have US, Iran set to reopen waterway
Article Text:
Iran says Hormuz will reopen only after US accepts its demands, while Washington seeks unrestricted commercial shipping. (Donald Trump, Iran President Masoud Pezeshkian)

What Iran wants before reopening the strait

1. An end to US threats against Iran

2. An end to US military action

3. Withdrawal of US naval and air forces involved in the blockade

4. Compensation for damage caused during the conflict

5. Lifting of sanctions

6. Unfreezing Iranian assets

7. No US interference in regional negotiations

What Iran and Oman are negotiating

What the US wants

Washington also wants unrestricted commercial shipping

The US wants Iran to fulfil its commitments

Why the Iran-Oman deal is not enough

What could unlock the Strait of Hormuz

Pezeshkian signals room for negotiations

Iran has made clear that a deal with Oman on a new shipping arrangement for the Strait of Hormuz will not, by itself, reopen the strategic waterway. Tehran says the strait will reopen only after the United States accepts a broader set of Iranian conditions, while Washington has indicated that it is prepared to lift its blockade of Iranian ports once commercial shipping resumes without impediments.The competing positions have emerged as Iran and Oman move closer to an agreement on a new shipping protocol for the Strait of Hormuz, a narrow but critical maritime route through which a fifth of the world's oil and gas shipments passed before the conflict.Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran and Muscat were "very close" to an agreement on a new arrangement for shipping through the strait. However, he made clear that the agreement with Oman would not be sufficient on its own to reopen the waterway.The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has also rejected suggestions that the reopening of the strait is simply a matter for the Iran-Oman negotiations.IRGC spokesperson Hossein Mohebbi said the reopening of the waterway was "contingent upon the United States accepting Iran's conditions and has no connection to the Iran-Oman negotiations."He later said, "Whenever the United States accepts Iran’s conditions, the Strait of Hormuz will certainly be reopened," according to Iran's Tasnim news agency.The statements point to a much broader dispute than the technical question of how ships will navigate the strait. At the centre of the disagreement are US military operations, sanctions, Iranian assets, compensation for wartime damage and control over shipping through one of the world's most important energy corridors.Iran's demands extend beyond an agreement with Oman on shipping arrangements. According to Al Jazeera, Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, has outlined several conditions for reopening the waterway.Tehran wants Washington to stop threatening Iran and end what it sees as continued US pressure against the country.For Iran, reopening the strait is therefore linked to the broader security situation. Tehran has argued that maritime arrangements cannot be separated from the military conflict and the wider confrontation with Washington.Iran wants the United States to halt military action against Iran and its regional allies.The demand comes after months of conflict involving US and Israeli attacks on Iran and Iranian retaliation against US interests and bases in the region.Tehran's position is that a return to normal commercial shipping must be accompanied by a wider reduction in military confrontation.Iran has also demanded the withdrawal of US naval and air forces involved in the blockade.The presence of US forces around the waterway has become a central point of contention. Washington has said it controls the blockade and has linked any lifting of restrictions to Iran meeting its commitments.US President Donald Trump said the US Navy was leading the blockade and that Washington controlled it."I don't want to say it has been... it's sort of open right now. We have a thing called the blockade headed up by the US Navy, and we control it. But they can always shoot something or drop a mine... if you have one mine sitting out there, you sort of mess things up because people don't want to take their billion-dollar boats and accidentally get hit by a mine. But I think we're doing very well. I am involved in the negotiations. I think we are doing fine... it could be soon."Another major Iranian demand is compensation from the US for damage caused during the conflict.Iran has indicated that an agreement on shipping cannot be separated from the economic and physical damage it says has resulted from the US military campaign.Araghchi has specifically said that US compensation to Iran would have to be addressed before the strait could reopen.Iran also wants US sanctions imposed on the country to be lifted.Sanctions have been one of the principal tools used by Washington to pressure Tehran. For Iran, their removal would represent a broader economic component of any agreement to end the confrontation.Tehran has also demanded that Iranian assets frozen under US sanctions be released.This would give Iran access to funds that have been restricted as part of the sanctions regime and would form another major element of the economic settlement Tehran is seeking.The IRGC has separately insisted that Washington must stop interfering in regional negotiations.Mohebbi said reopening the strait depended on "specific mechanisms and conditions" and was separate from the negotiations between Iran and Oman.This is important because Oman has been playing a role in discussions over the shipping arrangement. Iran appears to be treating the Oman talks as a mechanism for resolving the technical and legal aspects of maritime traffic, while insisting that the United States must separately meet its political and military conditions.Iran and Oman are working on a new arrangement governing shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.Araghchi said the previous shipping traffic separation scheme was no longer acceptable to Tehran. Iran is therefore discussing a temporary route with Oman while technical and legal questions surrounding a permanent route are resolved.The proposed arrangement is aimed at allowing commercial shipping to resume while addressing Iran's concerns over how vessels enter and leave the Persian Gulf.According to Reuters, a proposed deal could give Iran control over ships entering the Gulf through the strait. A senior Iranian source and two regional officials were cited as saying this would represent a major concession to Tehran.However, US officials have repeatedly indicated that Washington would not accept Iran controlling access to the world's most important energy trade route.This disagreement over who controls shipping is therefore one of the most difficult elements of the proposed arrangement.Washington's position is different from Tehran's.The US has indicated that it wants commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz to resume without impediments and has tied the lifting of its blockade to Iran fulfilling its commitments.A US official told Reuters, "There is progress between Oman and Iran on the strait, and we expect a deal soon. Once the deal is announced to restore commercial shipping without impediments, the United States will lift the blockade of Iranian ports."The official added, "As always, US actions will continue to be performance-based and tied to Iran’s implementation of its commitments."This suggests that Washington sees the reopening of the strait as part of a reciprocal process. Iran would have to meet its commitments before the US takes corresponding steps.The US position centres on restoring normal commercial traffic through the waterway.Washington does not appear willing to accept an arrangement under which Iran has unrestricted authority to decide which ships can enter or leave the Persian Gulf.The issue is particularly important because the strait is a global energy chokepoint. Disruption there affects oil and gas shipments far beyond Iran and the Gulf region.Washington has also made clear that any concessions would be conditional.The US official said American actions would remain "performance-based", meaning Washington would expect Iran to implement agreed measures before the US follows through on its own commitments.Trump has also linked the broader negotiations to the US objective of preventing Iran from possessing a nuclear weapon.The Strait of Hormuz connects the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and the wider Arabian Sea. Its strategic importance comes from the enormous volume of energy that passes through the narrow waterway.Before the conflict, the strait carried around a fifth of the world's oil and gas shipments.That makes any prolonged disruption a global economic issue rather than simply a dispute between Iran and the US.When shipping is threatened, tanker operators face higher insurance costs, longer routes and the risk of vessels being attacked or detained. Energy prices can rise as traders anticipate shortages, adding to inflationary pressure.Iran's actions around the waterway have therefore attracted intense international attention.The UAE said on Saturday that Iran had attacked a carrier affiliated with its state oil company with a missile while it was transiting the Strait of Hormuz. No injuries were reported. Iranian authorities did not immediately comment on the allegation.Abu Dhabi National Oil Company has also said that 15 of its vessels had been struck while transiting the strait since the beginning of the conflict, resulting in one crew member being killed and 20 injured.The central problem is that Iran and the US appear to be negotiating different parts of the same crisis.Iran's position: A shipping agreement with Oman can resolve navigation and maritime arrangements, but the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until Washington accepts Tehran's wider political, military and economic conditions.US position: Washington expects Iran and Oman to reach an arrangement allowing normal commercial shipping, after which the US would lift its blockade of Iranian ports, subject to Iran fulfilling its commitments.This creates a major gap between the two sides. For Iran, reopening the strait is part of a broader settlement with the United States.For Washington, reopening the waterway is more closely tied to Iran's implementation of commitments and the restoration of unrestricted commercial shipping.A deal would likely require progress on several issues at the same time.First, Iran and Oman would need to settle the technical and legal framework governing shipping. Tehran has said the previous traffic separation system is no longer acceptable and wants a temporary arrangement while a permanent system is negotiated.Second, Iran and the US would need to resolve the question of military activity around the waterway. Tehran wants US forces involved in the blockade withdrawn, while Washington wants assurances that commercial vessels can move safely without interference.Third, the two sides would have to address the economic issues raised by Iran, including compensation, sanctions and frozen Iranian assets.Finally, there would need to be agreement on who has authority over vessels using the strait. This could prove especially difficult if Washington opposes any arrangement that gives Tehran effective control over access to the waterway.Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has indicated that Tehran sees an opportunity for diplomacy, even while maintaining that Iran will not surrender what it considers its rights.In a post on X, he said: "The best time to reach an agreement is the current situation. On the path to peace, we will not compromise on the rights of the Iranian nation. The government's main reliance is on domestic capacities and the people. The necessity of a compassionate approach toward the people | People are in two categories; either they are your religious brothers, or they are equal to you in creation."Pezeshkian's comments suggest that Iran remains open to negotiations, but Tehran sees the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz as part of a wider agreement with the US.For Iran, reopening the strait depends on an end to US military action and threats, withdrawal of US forces involved in the blockade, compensation for wartime damage, lifting of sanctions, unfreezing of Iranian assets and an end to US interference in regional talks.The US, meanwhile, wants commercial shipping to resume without restrictions and expects Iran to fulfil its commitments before Washington takes further steps. It also opposes giving Iran unilateral control over the waterway.Oman is trying to help the two sides reach an agreement on shipping through the strait. However, Iran has made clear that an Iran-Oman deal alone will not be enough to reopen the waterway.
Article Summary: Iran says Hormuz will reopen only after US accepts its demands, while Washington seeks unrestricted commercial shipping. Iran and Oman move closer to an agreement on a new shipping protocol for the strait. Iran wants Washington to stop threatening Iran and end what it sees as continued US pressure against the country.

Article Title: Watch: Accident victim's fractured leg tied with carton at Bihar Hospital; probe ordered
Article Text:
Kunal was riding his motorcycle when he met with an accident near Harsain Bridge. He suffered a fracture in his right leg.





PATNA: A road accident victim at Manjhaul Sub-Divisional Hospital in Bihar's Begusarai district was allegedly treated by immobilising his fractured leg with pieces of a medicine carton instead of a plaster, triggering outrage after a video of the procedure went viral on social media.The patient, identified as Kunal Kumar, is a resident of Maheshwara village under the Nawkothi police station limits. The incident took place on the evening of August 3.According to his family members, Kunal was riding his motorcycle when he met with an accident near Harsain Bridge. He suffered a fracture in his right leg and was taken to Manjhaul Sub-Divisional Hospital by locals and relatives.At the hospital, staff on duty allegedly placed two pieces of a medicine carton on either side of his fractured leg and secured them tightly with rope and bandages. After administering first aid, doctors referred him to Sadar Hospital in Begusarai.In the viral video, Kunal can be seen lying on a hospital bed with a pharmaceutical carton tied around his injured leg.When contacted, Manjhaul Hospital in-charge Dr Abhinav Priyadarshi defended the procedure. He admitted to the shortcomings but said the treatment was in line with medical protocol."What you are calling a 'koot' or carton is called a splint in medical science.When a bone is broken, it is necessary to immobilise that part to prevent further internal damage," Dr Priyadarshi said.He said there was no orthopaedic doctor or dresser available at the time, and the hospital also lacked plaster facilities."To relieve the patient's pain and prevent the leg from moving while shifting him to a higher centre, using available material as a splint is justified under medical protocol," he added.Begusarai civil surgeon Dr Ashok Kumar said he had taken note of the viral video."I have received information about the incident. The video has gone viral. I will get it investigated, and if anyone is found guilty, action will be taken," he said.Dr Kumar added that using a carton as a temporary splint is recognised in medical practice for emergency first aid. "But if this was done at the hospital, it will be investigated," he said.When asked, Manjhaul Hospital In-charge Dr Abhinav Priyadarshi defended the procedure. He admitted to the shortcomings but said it was done as per medical protocol.“What you are calling ‘koot’ or carton is called a splint in medical science. When a bone is broken, it is necessary to immobilize that part to prevent further internal damage,” Dr Priyadarshi said.He said there was no orthopaedic doctor or dresser available at the time and there was no arrangement for plaster either.“To give the patient relief from pain and to prevent the leg from moving while shifting him to a higher centre, tying a splint with available material is justified under medical protocol,” he added.
Article Summary: Kunal Kumar was riding his motorcycle when he met with an accident near Harsain Bridge. He suffered a fracture in his right leg and was taken to Manjhaul Sub- Divisional Hospital. Staff allegedly placed two pieces of a medicine carton on either side of his fractured leg and secured them tightly with rope and bandages.

Article Title: 'We demand that NTA be dissolved': CJP's Ashutosh Ranka on CBI charge sheet in NEET 2026 case
Article Text:
CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka said the new body should have permanent staff and a system for proper auditing of every examination it conducts.





NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP ) has demanded that the National Testing Agency (NTA) be dissolved and converted into a national technical testing commission following the Central Bureau of Investigation's (CBI) chargesheet in the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak case.CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka said the new body should have permanent staff and a system for proper auditing of every examination it conducts.“I just came to know that CBI has filed a chargesheet in the NEET 2026 case which involves a lot of NTA officers,” Ranka said.He also demanded a thorough investigation into all paper leaks reported in the country over the past few years, including the NEET-UG 2024 and NEET-UG 2025 cases, and called for those responsible to be brought to justice.Ranka said the government should address what he described as structural problems affecting the country's examination system, including examination infrastructure and vendors involved in conducting exams.“It is imperative that the government takes steps to solve these structural issues that are plaguing the systems of this country, not just NTA but the entire exam system,” he said.“The exam infrastructure which includes the vendors have to be audited properly and it has to be made sure that the country doesn't see any more paper leaks,” he added.What does the CBI chargesheet allege?The CBI has alleged that the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak was part of a coordinated, multi-state conspiracy in which NTA-appointed subject experts allegedly accessed confidential examination papers and passed them on to middlemen and coaching operators for money.In a chargesheet filed before the special CBI court at Delhi's Rouse Avenue, the agency named 13 accused, including three NTA-appointed subject experts: Botany specialist Manisha Gurunath Mandhare, Chemistry expert Prahlad Vithalrao Kulkarni and Physics expert Manisha Sanjay Havaldar.According to the CBI, the leaked questions were circulated through a network of intermediaries before allegedly reaching candidates who paid for access to them.The accused have been booked under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), the Prevention of Corruption Act and the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024.The agency alleged that forensic examination of seized mobile phones, pen drives and other electronic devices recovered PDF and image files containing NEET-UG 2026 questions.Investigators said the files were exchanged through Telegram, WhatsApp and other messaging platforms several days before the examination.The chargesheet names Tejas Shah, Shivraj Motegaonkar, Dr Manoj Shirure, Manisha Sanjay Waghmare, Dhananjay Lokhande, Shubham Khairnar, Yash Yadav, Mangilal Biwal, Dinesh Biwal and Vikas Biwal in addition to the three NTA experts.The CBI has alleged that the accused played different roles in sourcing, circulating and distributing the leaked questions and handling financial transactions.The agency's investigation also included statements from candidates and their family members.In one instance, the CBI alleged that a candidate and her father were offered access to the NEET-UG 2026 question paper for Rs 4 lakh, along with coaching support and offline revision classes conducted by one of the NTA subject experts.The CBI said forensic evidence, chat records, recovered documents and witness statements support its allegations of criminal conspiracy, abuse of official position by public servants and illegal circulation of confidential examination material before the NEET-UG 2026 examination.
Article Summary: CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka said the new body should have permanent staff and a system for proper auditing of every examination it conducts. Ranka also demanded a thorough investigation into all paper leaks reported in the country over the past few years, including the NEET-UG 2024 and NEet-UG 2025 cases.

Article Title: Asmongold Twitch suspension: Tectone backs streamer’s ‘shoot whoever’ border comments after explosive backlash
Article Text:
Asmongold Twitch suspension: Tectone backs streamer’s ‘shoot whoever’ border comments after explosive backlash

John "Tectone" defends Zack "Asmongold" during his Rumble livestream

Twitch suspends Zack "Asmongold" secondary channel following Ceuta migration comments

Popular streamer John “Tectone” has publicly defended his former OTK teammate Zack “Asmongold” following a massive online controversy regarding illegal immigration and border control. The backlash started after Asmongold made extreme statements about migrants during an August 3 livestream while reacting to a YouTube video. Shortly after the incident, Twitch temporarily banned Asmongold’s secondary channel, Zackrawrr, on August 7 for violating platform rules. While Twitch did not officially state the exact reason for the suspension, Tectone took to his own livestream on Rumble to support Asmongold, arguing that his words had been misunderstood.Instead of distancing himself from the controversy, John "Tectone" spoke openly about the situation during a recent broadcast on Rumble. He argued that Zack "Asmongold" was not trying to promote harm, but was instead pointing out how desperate circumstances force nations into tough decisions. Tectone explained that the comments were focused on taking harsh actions to stop women and children from being placed in ongoing danger by people crossing borders illegally.Explaining his position to viewers, Tectone said:“Now this can sound heartless. ... Illegal criminals from Africa are forcibly invading other countries, and they're using the women and children. ... The problem is, an extreme measure needs to be taken once to ensure that more women and children are not being put into the line of fire and the line of danger in perpetuity”He further claimed that world governments are facing continuous pressure when vulnerable groups are involved in conflict zones. He added:“We don't want to do this, but it's our only choice for the safety of our countries. They did the same thing in Iran, where they put, and they built an elementary school on top of their military base, so if anybody retaliated against their terrorist activity, they would say, 'Oh my God, they're bombing the children.’ They are doing emotional blackmail on not just the USA but everyone on this Earth.”According to Tectone, Asmongold’s message was essentially that people crossing illegally force harsh reactions, stating, “What he said was these people are forcing our hand to do something horrible, but we must do that for the safety of our people.”The ongoing drama started on August 3, 2026, when Zack "Asmongold" was reviewing a YouTube clip about migration issues in Ceuta, Spain. During his stream, Asmongold made extreme statements about stopping unauthorized border crossings, saying that force should be used even if women and children are present. He claimed migrants use families as shields to enter countries without permission.While responding to his audience, Asmongold shared his view on border enforcement:“This is emotional blackmail. Right? You can't shoot these people; they have kids with them. Well, then, don't bring your kids. If you don't want to get shot, then don't bring your f***ing kids! It's really simple. 'You mean you'd shoot adults and deport the kids? Right?' Well, I'd shoot whoever. Yeah, I'd shoot whoever. I mean, if it's kids, women, men, anybody, just shoot them. They're going to stop coming over, because if you don't do that, they will use children and women as shields to get themselves over. ”Days after the stream, on August 7, Twitch suspended Asmongold’s main active account, Zackrawrr, which holds about 2.4 million followers. Twitch cited Community Guidelines violations without giving specific details. The account cannot stream live right now, though old videos remain up. With Tectone stepping in, debate online keeps growing.
Article Summary: John "Tectone" has publicly defended his former OTK teammate Zack "Asmongold" following a massive online controversy regarding illegal immigration and border control. The backlash started after Asmongold made extreme statements about migrants during an August 3 livestream while reacting to a YouTube video. Tectone explained that the comments were focused on taking harsh actions to stop women and children from being placed in ongoing danger by people crossing borders illegally.

Fresh reports suggest David and Victoria Beckham came remarkably close to crossing paths with their eldest son, Brooklyn Beckham, and his wife, Nicola Peltz, during separate holidays in the South of France. Article Title: US appeals court halts Trump's $400 million ballroom project, grants 14 days for Supreme Court appeal
Article Text:
A US federal appeals court on Friday ordered President Donald Trump's administration to halt construction of a proposed $400 million ballroom at the White House (AP image)

A US federal appeals court on Friday ordered President Donald Trump's administration to halt construction of a proposed $400 million ballroom at the White House, dealing a significant setback to the president's plan to reshape the historic complex.In a 2-1 ruling, the Washington-based US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit upheld a preliminary injunction obtained by the National Trust for Historic Preservation, which challenged the project after the administration demolished the White House's East Wing and began building a 90,000-square-foot ballroom without congressional approval, cites Reuters.The appeals court, however, put its order on hold for 14 days, giving the Trump administration time to appeal to the US Supreme Court.The ruling comes after US District Judge Richard Leon had twice blocked above-ground construction while allowing underground work to continue. Leon ruled that "no federal statute comes close to giving the President" the authority to construct the ballroom without approval from Congress.The Trump administration has defended the project, saying the ballroom is needed to host large formal events while improving security at the White House.The ballroom is among several initiatives by Trump aimed at reshaping government buildings and national landmarks in Washington.During arguments before the appeals court in June, Justice Department lawyer Yaakov Roth argued that the judiciary had no role in reviewing the privately funded project."The courts have no role" in weighing the project, Roth said, adding that the preservation group's "architectural preference" against the ballroom should not outweigh national security concerns. He argued the former East Wing left "the president and others in the White House vulnerable to attack."Opposing the administration, Thaddeus Heuer, counsel for the National Trust for Historic Preservation, said the issue was not aesthetics but legal procedure. "They just don't want to go to Congress," Heuer told the court.Trump has repeatedly defended the ballroom and its rising cost, which has nearly doubled from initial estimates. In a post on Truth Social last month, he said the price increased because "it is approximately twice the size, and a far higher quality, than the original proposal," adding that "it will be magnificent, safe, and secure!"The ballroom case follows another recent legal setback for the administration after a judge ruled that Trump's name had been unlawfully added to the exterior of the Kennedy Center and ordered its removal.
Article Summary: A US federal appeals court on Friday ordered President Donald Trump's administration to halt construction of a proposed $400 million ballroom at the White House. In a 2-1 ruling, the court upheld a preliminary injunction obtained by the National Trust for Historic Preservation. The appeals court, however, put its order on hold for 14 days, giving the Trump administration time to appeal to the US Supreme Court.

Article Title: Indian expat from Kerala killed in Dubai gas cylinder blast; colleague recalls moments before explosion
Article Text:
Shijin Paul/Image: X

Colleague recounts fire before blast

Explosion struck during firefighting efforts

An Indian-origin man from Kerala was killed in a gas cylinder explosion at a car showroom on Sheikh Zayed Road in Dubai on Monday, the Indian Consulate in Dubai confirmed, Gulf News reported.The victim was identified as Shijin Paul, 27, from Kottarakkara in Kerala's Kollam district.A relative told the outlet that Shijin succumbed to his injuries at a hospital after the explosion."I was informed by his company about the blast. Unfortunately, he had passed away by the time I reached the hospital," the relative said.Shijin worked as the showroom's multimedia marketing specialist, handling social media and videography. According to his family, he had joined the company in November. He is survived by his parents and wife.A co-worker who witnessed the incident said employees rushed outside after colleagues noticed a fire on the premises."Some of us, including Shijin and I, went out of our showroom after some of our colleagues alerted us about a fire," Abid, a photographer who worked with Shijin, told the newspaper."There were people from several shops nearby too, not just from our showroom.Many people came running after spotting the fire."Abid said the flames appeared to have broken out near a gate close to neighbouring auto service workshops."There is a gate in one corner of the showroom, and the fire started somewhere there. There are some auto service companies next to our showroom, and the fire was near their location."According to Abid, people at the scene attempted to contain the fire with extinguishers before the cylinder exploded."People were trying to put out the fire with fire extinguishers. The explosion occurred while efforts were underway to douse the fire. Everyone ran away," he said.He added that he did not immediately realise Shijin had been caught in the blast."I don't know who all got hit. I got to know about his death later," Abid said.The Indian Consulate said it remains in contact with Shijin's family and the authorities to provide support following the incident.
Article Summary: Shijin Paul, 27, from Kottarakkara in Kerala's Kollam district, died in the blast. He worked as the showroom's multimedia marketing specialist, handling social media and videography. A co-worker who witnessed the incident said employees rushed outside after colleagues noticed a fire on the premises.

Article Title: Hazaribag man drowns while fishing in lake
Article Text:

A man drowned in a lake of Hazaribag city while fishing, police said on Monday. The deceased was identified as Mohammad Kalim (50), a resident of Sardar Chowk Mohalla. Officer in-charge of the Lohsighna police station Rohit Kerketta said, “Family members of the deceased told police that he had left home on Sunday morning as usual to catch fish in the lake but did not return till late in the night. They began a search and found his fishing gear and a tiffin box on the bank of the lake. His body was later found floating in the lake. An investigation is under way to ascertain the circumstances leading to the death.”
Article Summary: The deceased was identified as Mohammad Kalim (50), a resident of Sardar Chowk Mohalla.
